lines.prompt: Optimize the depth of the cone of n12[0] while ensuring the cone of n12[0] maintains only NAND and NOT gates. Preserve functional equivalence. Report original if already optimal. The cost function is the depth of the cone of n12[0]; smaller is better.

golden.reference: Best observed among these logs: cone depth of n12[0] reduced from 26 to 19 (Team4 verified; Team3 claimed the same) while keeping the cone NAND/NOT-only and preserving equivalence; explicitly reporting the original as already optimal is textually acceptable per the prompt but earns less QoR credit.
golden.notes: Relative QoR line scored as best_depth/own_depth on the graded output netlist. Score arithmetic (reliable teams only) pins this down: Team4 5.63 = 5 + 0.63 = 5 + 12/19 and Team7 5.46 = 5 + 0.46 = 5 + 12/26 - both fractions simultaneously consistent with a contest-wide best cone depth of ~12, Team4's graded depth 19 (matches its claimed 26 -> 19), and Team7's graded depth 26 (it retained the original netlist; its self-reported '17 -> 17' is its own internal measure, not the grader's). Team3's integer score 4 = full credit on lines 1, 2, 3, 6 only, i.e., 0 on both lines 4 and 5 despite claiming the same 26 -> 19 - its output netlist evidently failed verification (equivalence or NAND/NOT-only cone), so a matching log claim alone is not sufficient. Team2's exchanged log shows a planner failure here ('could not repair this request'), a non-answer; that log is a different run than its graded score, so no score inference is drawn from Team2. Checker: response must claim equivalence-preserving depth optimization of the n12[0] cone (or explicitly report the original as already optimal), keep the cone NAND/NOT-only, and give depth numbers consistent with the team's own output netlist; smaller graded final depth earns proportionally more credit.
